clue.text: Scheme to avoid returning after school

indicators.note: after places the backwards piece behind the abbreviation for school
returning means the word for 'to avoid' is read backwards

parts.note: to elude something is to avoid it

explanation.surface: A pupil's plan to dodge going back to class once lessons are over.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable or programme of planned events is a scheme in the sense of an arrangement.

clue.text: Spies supporting very large party

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece supporting another sits below it, so the spies come after the word for very

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
the CIA is the American spy agency
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Secret agents propping up an enormous political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A party in the sense of a get-together or gathering is also called a social, a noun use.

clue.text: One trapped inside unfortunately who endlessly uses iron?

definitions.text: One trapped inside unfortunately who endlessly uses iron?

indicators.note: trapped inside says the letter for one is enclosed within the other letters
unfortunately signals the letters of who and the shortened uses are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word uses is dropped

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sympathetic picture of a home-bound woman stuck indoors doing the ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' scrambles who plus the trimmed uses into HOUSEW. The whole clue also describes the answer, an old stereotype of someone stuck at home ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional homemaker kept indoors doing chores such as pressing laundry fits the whole clue's description.

clue.text: Editor picked up girl's broadcast

indicators.note: in a down answer picked up means the abbreviation is lifted and read from bottom to top

parts.note: Clare is a girl's name; the 's joins it to the definition

explanation.surface: An editor overheard a young woman's words being transmitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' and 'broadcast' both look like radio talk; here 'picked up' reverses ED to DE, and 'broadcast' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news is to announce or proclaim it publicly, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: John almost set free

parts.note: john is slang, mainly American, for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word set is cut off

explanation.surface: A man called John has nearly been released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name but is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something free is to turn it loose, so the two adjectives match as synonyms.

clue.text: Rarely succeeded with student in contrary manner

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: in puts the learner letter inside the backwards manner
contrary means the word for manner is turned the opposite way

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
L is for learner, the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: Someone seldom got on well while studying in an awkward, contrary way.
explanation.walkthrough: MODE backwards is EDOM; L goes in to give ELDOM after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning not often, a straightforward synonym pair.

clue.text: Tied up — and about to tie the knot

definitions.meaning: busy or occupied, as a phone line or a person can be
betrothed, due to be married soon

explanation.definitionFit: Busy is one sense of the adjective; promised in marriage is the other, both standard meanings.

clue.text: Plan to put daughter on basic river craft

indicators.note: in a down answer on means placed above, so daughter comes first

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
a raft is the simplest kind of boat

explanation.surface: A scheme to set a girl afloat on a simple boat downstream.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline of something, much like a plan.

clue.text: Reasonable chair

definitions.meaning: sensible and not extreme, as in reasonable views
to preside over a debate or meeting, as a chairperson does

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means not extreme; as a verb it means to preside over a discussion.

clue.text: Found cereal is edible, to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has discovered that breakfast cereal can actually be eaten, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Found in the sense of discovered or understood, as in 'found it was true', is a synonym of the past tense.

clue.text: Doctor changed for lunch that's headed by the Queen

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor switched something around for a midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is the instruction to rearrange; 'changed' is part of the letters. The clue predates 2022, when the monarch was a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The British monarch is Supreme Governor of the established church in England, so it is headed by the sovereign.

clue.text: State how old one is? That's mean

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
one's age is how old one is

explanation.surface: Asking someone to declare their years is thought rather unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like 'unkind' but is the arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the typical value found by summing and dividing, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Beggar ignoring first cause of fire?

indicators.note: ignoring first means the opening letter of the word for beggar is dropped

parts.note: beggar and blighter are both mild British terms of abuse for a rascal

explanation.surface: A tramp who disregards the first thing that might start a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHTER, an old British insult like 'beggar', loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A small device for igniting cigarettes or stoves is something that starts a fire, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Food course hospital dropped off takes the edge off illnesses

indicators.note: dropped off means the hospital letter is removed from the course

parts.note: a dish is one course of a meal
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to ease pain is to take the edge off it

explanation.surface: Delivering a meal to a ward helps make patients' sickness more bearable.
explanation.walkthrough: DISH less H gives DIS, then EASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name medical disorders or sicknesses, so they are plural synonyms.

clue.text: Changing dress at home before golf

indicators.note: before places the dress and home pieces ahead of the golf letter

parts.note: a shift is a simple straight dress
in means at home, as in 'staying in'
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone getting changed out of their clothes at home before a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifting and changing both mean altering position or moving from one state to another.

clue.text: Question friend about eating over time

indicators.note: eating means the backwards friend swallows the over letter
about means the word for friend is turned round

parts.note: bud is short for buddy, a friend
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Quizzing a pal about a meal they had a while ago.
explanation.walkthrough: BUD reversed is DUB; it eats O to give DOUB, then T. In cricket an over is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: To question something is to call it into doubt, both verbs meaning to be unsure of.

clue.text: Erratic aunt nicer when drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt becomes friendlier but less steady after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic and uncertain both describe something unpredictable or changeable, close synonyms.

clue.text: That is Victor in pain, head of department realised

indicators.note: in puts the 'that is' and Victor letters inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of department

explanation.surface: A wounded winner named Victor is finally noticed by his departmental boss.
explanation.walkthrough: IE and V go into ACHE to make ACHIEVE, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an ambition is to fulfil or accomplish it, so the past tenses are synonyms.

clue.text: The man wears animal fleece

indicators.note: wears means the man is wrapped in the animal, so the animal goes around him

parts.note: a cat is an animal
he is the pronoun for the man

explanation.surface: A man dressed in an animal-hide coat, or a shearling fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a woolly garment but is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them out of money, a slang synonym for the verb.

clue.text: One educates revolutionary about race? On the contrary

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other
On the contrary flips the stated arrangement, so race goes around revolutionary

parts.note: to tear is to race along
Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel lecturing on a contest, or perhaps on ethnicity.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, CHE would surround TEAR; 'On the contrary' reverses that, giving TEA(CHE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: A school instructor is someone who educates, so the clause works as a description of the noun.

clue.text: Type of speech that's reported in dreadful court

parts.note: dire means dreadful

explanation.surface: A grammarian describes reported speech heard in a terrible courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' looks like an anagram signal but just means DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls speech relayed in the third person, not quoted, indirect speech, a standard term.

clue.text: Wheel radius to change gradually

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry
to evolve is to develop gradually

explanation.surface: A wheel's spoke length altering little by little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheel' looks like a noun but is the verb, to turn in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn round in a circle, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Possible source of steam bloke heard

indicators.note: heard says the word for bloke is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a bloke, a man

explanation.surface: A man was overheard talking about where steam might come from.
explanation.walkthrough: GEEZER is British slang for a man; in British speech the hot spring or gas water-heater is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A geothermal spout or a water heater both give off steam, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Mo isn't running with a new top on today

indicators.note: running suggests the letters move about into a new order
top on picks the first letter of today

explanation.surface: A runner called Mo is not out jogging in a new shirt today.
explanation.walkthrough: ISNT rearranged gives INST, then A, N and T. 'Mo' looks like a runner's name, perhaps Mo Farah, but is short for moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mo is British informal shorthand for moment, as in 'half a mo', meaning a very short time.

clue.text: Avoids barbarians after start of skirmish

indicators.note: after places the barbarians behind the opening letter
start of picks the first letter of skirmish

parts.note: the Huns were the archetypal barbarian invaders

explanation.surface: Someone keeps clear of savage invaders once fighting breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun someone is to keep away from them, so both verbs mean deliberately keep clear.

clue.text: Adore holding son back

indicators.note: holding means the word for adore contains the son letter

parts.note: to revere is to adore or venerate
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent clinging lovingly to a child to keep him from leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction for the son but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse a car is to back it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Transported heroin, not ecstasy, for cash

indicators.note: transported means the remaining letters are carried into a new arrangement
not means the ecstasy letter is removed from heroin

parts.note: E is the drug slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler moved heroin rather than ecstasy, in exchange for money.
explanation.walkthrough: HEROIN without E leaves HROIN, rearranged by 'Transported'. RHINO is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is a dated British slang word for money, a slang synonym for cash.

clue.text: Was having allium prepared, notes man?

indicators.note: prepared suggests ingredients made ready, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone had onion or garlic cooked for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: An allium is the onion family. Ralph Vaughan Williams was an English composer, so 'notes man' is a cryptic way of saying composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer is a man whose trade is musical notes, and this English composer wrote The Lark Ascending.

clue.text: Leave pudding after losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means one of the middle letters of the word for pudding is dropped

parts.note: pudding is the British word for dessert

explanation.surface: Walking out of dinner after the dessert proved disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: DESSERT drops one of its central S's.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert a place or person is to leave or abandon it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: No resistance after Tory runs for leader

indicators.note: after puts the 'no' and resistance pieces behind the Tory and runs

parts.note: Michael Gove is a prominent Conservative (Tory) politician
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A Conservative standing for party leader meets no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory' is the politician Michael Gove, not a general word for a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A state governor or a prison governor is a person in charge, so the word works as a synonym for a leader.
